title: Descent extends affine cartesian determinant data to arbitrary schemes
statement: Given normalized derived pullback coherence [lem-trf-two-term-determinant-pullback-coherence] and an affine cartesian determinant system with compatible local exterior, zero and evaluation families [def-trf-affine-determinant-interfaces], there exists determinant-functor data on every scheme, with its model and zero comparisons, evaluation, and coherent arbitrary pullback. This is a conditional descent result: the input affine system is supplied, rather than constructed here. No global derived determinant functor is a hypothesis.

source.place: Tags 0FJX and 0FJY, affine gluing argument; descent.tex Tag 023T.

proof.text: Restrict each object to an affine open cover. Source membership is preserved by the proved arbitrary pullback theorem. For affine refinements of overlaps use the supplied affine pullback comparisons and κ to define transition maps. Naturality, identity and composition show compatibility under further restriction and the cocycle equation. Equal sheaf maps are detected on affine bases, so the maps glue over non-affine overlaps too.

An open cover is fpqc: its maps are flat and an affine open has a finite principal refinement. The explicit descentGlue construction glues the local modules. Descent and its full faithfulness prove invertibility and glue all morphisms; faithfulness proves functor laws and independence of refinements. The local_model_naturality and local_zero_naturality fields make the specified model/zero maps descend. local_acyclic descends the evaluation equation.

For any morphism refine its domain by affine opens mapping into affine model opens. Glue the given affine cartesian comparisons there. Derived restriction is identified by the flat-model and affine tensor comparisons. The affine naturality and unit/composition equations, with κ coherence, prove all global equations after applying faithful restriction.

mathlib_searches.query: determinant functor two term perfect complexes invertible sheaf pullback
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits about free module pullback isomorphisms; none constructs determinant functors or affine descent. For the Tor-window search, DerivedCategory.exists_iso_Q_obj_of_isGE_of_isLE gives a cohomologically bounded complex, without finite locally free terms. The existing finite-free residue model in our library supplies the stronger input.
Zero hits. The separate "Perfect", "Tor" query returned unrelated perfect groups, perfect closures and graph matchings.

Two hits in Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Complex/Determinant.lean concern complex numbers, not complexes. The additional leftAdjointCompIso search found the mate/composition API used in the proved normalized-coherence argument. No determinant construction was found.

mathlib_searches.query: Determinant line of two term perfect complexes compatible with affine base change and descent
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits: LinearMap.det, IsBaseChange.det_endHom, LinearEquiv.det_baseChange, LinearMap.det_baseChange and related scalar determinants. These are endomorphism determinants, not determinant lines of complexes or compatible gluing data. The queried theorem types do not provide the required construction.

from.place: Proof (1)--(2), semistable-alteration input in the nearby-cycle branch: ILO Exposé X, Theorem 3.4, Step 3, invoking Temkin 2010, Theorems 1.5 and 1.1 for a semistable multipointed modification. Temkin proof component: Marked dualizing line bundle and contracted-component degrees. Auxiliary input: Local complete-intersection determinant adjunction underlying the marked dualizing construction, before the marking is inserted. Within the two-term determinant auxiliary: Descent extends affine cartesian determinant data to arbitrary schemes.

lean.statement:
theorem descend_affineTwoTermDeterminantData
    [∀ (X : Scheme.{u}) (U : X.Opens),
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    (κ : TwoTermDeterminantPullbackCoherence.{u, w})
    (A : AffineTwoTermDeterminantData κ) :
    Nonempty (TwoTermDeterminantFunctorData κ)
